items.stem: Which structure is present in prokaryotic cells but absent in eukaryotic cells?
choices: Circular DNA free in the cytoplasm
items.note: Prokaryotes have naked circular DNA (nucleoid); eukaryotic DNA is linear and enclosed in a nucleus. Both cell types have ribosomes and membranes.

items.stem: The function of the Golgi apparatus is to:
items.note: Golgi = protein processing and dispatch. Rough ER synthesises; mitochondria make ATP; the nucleus stores DNA.

items.stem: Which process moves molecules against their concentration gradient using ATP and membrane proteins?
items.note: Two keywords define active transport: against the gradient + ATP. Facilitated diffusion uses proteins but no ATP and follows the gradient.

items.stem: A cell is placed in a hypertonic solution. What happens to a plant cell?
choices: The membrane pulls away from the wall (plasmolysis)
items.note: Hypertonic = water leaves = plasmolysis in plants, crenation in animals. Hypotonic is when plant cells become turgid.

items.stem: Which phase of mitosis is characterised by chromosomes aligning on the equator of the cell?
items.note: Metaphase = middle. Anaphase = sister chromatids pulled apart; prophase = condensation + spindle forms.

items.stem: Cytokinesis in animal cells differs from plant cells because animal cells:
choices: Form a new cell wall first
items.note: Animals: cleavage furrow pinches the membrane. Plants: cell plate forms from vesicles (they have a wall, no furrow possible).

items.stem: Which property of phospholipids causes bilayer formation?
choices: Hydrophilic heads attracted to water, hydrophobic tails away from water
items.note: Amphipathic nature: heads face the aqueous sides, tails hide inside — the self-assembling bilayer.

items.stem: Which statement about the fluid mosaic model is correct?
choices: Proteins are fixed in a rigid membrane
Cholesterol decreases fluidity at high temperature and increases it at low temperature
Glycoproteins are found only on the inner face
items.note: Cholesterol is the buffer: restrains motion when warm, prevents packing when cold. Glycoproteins face the extracellular side.

items.stem: Stem cells are characterised by their ability to:
choices: Self-renew and differentiate into specialised cells
items.note: Two defining properties: self-renewal + potency (differentiation). Link to therapeutic uses (bone marrow transplants, Stargardt's disease trials).

items.stem: Which organelle would be most abundant in a pancreatic cell that secretes large amounts of digestive enzyme?
items.note: Protein secretion chain: ribosomes → rough ER → Golgi → vesicles. Structure–function links are common 1A marks.

items.stem: Osmosis is best defined as the movement of water:
choices: across a membrane from low to high water potential
across a partially permeable membrane from high to low water potential
against a concentration gradient using ATP
together with solutes through channel proteins
items.note: Water moves from higher to lower water potential — equivalently, toward the higher solute concentration. ATP and channels belong to active transport and facilitated diffusion respectively.

items.stem: Mitosis produces:
items.note: Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells (growth/repair). Meiosis: 4 different haploid cells (gametes). Mixing these up loses easy marks.

items.stem: Which is evidence supporting the cell theory?
choices: All observed living things are made of one or more cells
items.note: Cell theory: all living things are composed of cells; the cell is the basic unit; cells come from pre-existing cells. Viruses are the standard exception discussion.

items.stem: Facilitated diffusion differs from simple diffusion because it:
items.note: Protein-mediated, still passive (down the gradient, no ATP). Particular channels: aquaporins for water.

items.stem: During which stage of the cell cycle does DNA replication occur?
items.note: S = synthesis of DNA, between G1 and G2 in interphase. Checkpoints at G1, G2 and during mitosis control progression.

items.stem: Which structure controls what enters and leaves the cell?
items.note: The membrane is selectively permeable — the wall is fully permeable to most small molecules; the membrane is the gatekeeper.

items.stem: Endocytosis and exocytosis are alike because both:
items.note: Bulk transport of material in membrane vesicles — active processes requiring ATP.

items.stem: A magnified cell image shows a nucleus, mitochondria and a cellulose cell wall. The cell is:
items.note: Nucleus + cellulose wall + mitochondria = plant. Fungi walls are chitin, not cellulose; prokaryotes have no nucleus.

items.stem: Differentiated cells specialise because they:
items.note: All cells share the same genome; differential gene expression creates specialisation. Gene loss is wrong (except mature red blood cells' nuclei loss).

items.stem: Which experiment best demonstrates osmosis in living tissue?
choices: Weighing potato strips before and after immersion in sucrose solutions of different concentration
items.note: The classic potato/osmometer: mass change vs solution concentration gives an isotonic point. Data questions often reuse this setup in 1B.

items.stem: Explain how the properties of the phospholipid bilayer and membrane proteins together determine what can enter or leave a cell.
markscheme: Hydrophobic core of bilayer blocks large/polar molecules and ions (1)
Small non-polar molecules (O₂, CO₂) diffuse freely through the bilayer (1)
Channel/carrier proteins allow specific polar molecules/ions down the gradient (facilitated diffusion) (1)
Pump proteins use ATP to move substances against the gradient — selectivity + control (1)
items.tactic: Structure–function explanations: name the structure, state its property, then link to the consequence. Markers award per linked step.

items.stem: Potato strips of equal mass were placed in sucrose solutions of 0.0, 0.3 and 0.6 mol/dm³. After 1 hour masses were +12%, −1% and −15% respectively. Identify the approximate isotonic concentration and justify your answer.
markscheme: Zero mass change = no net water movement = isotonic (1)
Mass change crosses from +12% to −1% between 0.0 and 0.3, so isotonic point lies slightly below 0.3 mol/dm³ (1)
items.tactic: Data-response: state the principle (zero change = equilibrium), then read/interpolate the graph values, quoting units.
